## M18 -- Full System Prompts & In-Context Examples

**Goal:** Finalize all production-grade system prompt texts for Front and Back LLMs. The Front prompt is **dynamic** -- assembled per mode by `DynamicPromptBuilder` from `PROMPT_SECTIONS`, `MODE_EXAMPLES`, `AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS`, `CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS`, `DOMAIN_RULES`, and `SCENARIO_DATA_TEMPLATES`. The Back prompt is **monolithic** -- constant identity + dynamic task block. Both must be coherent: dynamically assembled sections must never contradict each other across any mode + affect + domain combination. The assembly flow is: `determine_mode() -> PromptMode -> MODE_SECTIONS[mode] -> list of section keys -> for each key: PROMPT_SECTIONS[key] -> concatenate -> append MODE_EXAMPLES[mode] -> append AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS[band] -> append CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS[depth] -> append DOMAIN_RULES[domain] -> append scenario_data -> append SS sections per SS_READ_CONFIGS[mode]`.
**Design Sections (V2):** 6.1 (Front prompt: PROMPT_SECTIONS, MODE_SECTIONS, DynamicPromptBuilder 12-step pipeline, tool allowlists, SS reads, MODE_EXAMPLES, SCENARIO_DATA_TEMPLATES, assembly order, affect tone blocks, clarification depth blocks, domain rules, anti-pattern subsets, token savings), 6.2 (Back prompt: identity, 8-step ReAct protocol, tool selection, safety, result format, ambiguity handling, anti-patterns, budget, in-context examples), 8.2-8.5 (multi-intent dispatch patterns), 10.7 (context budget), 14.3 (token savings validation)
**Depends On:** M09 (PromptMode enum, MODE_SECTIONS map, TOOL_ALLOWLIST, determine_mode(), SS_READ_CONFIGS per mode, SSReadConfig dataclass), M14 (AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS, CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS, DOMAIN_RULES, compute_affect_band()), M16 (orchestrator tier routing for Back budget tiers LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH), M17 (context budget management, DynamicPromptBuilder._compress_prompt(), pre-call budget check)
**Exit Criteria:**

- All 20 `PROMPT_SECTIONS` entries implemented with full production text matching Section 26.5.1 verbatim (IDENTITY, REACT_RHYTHM, REACT_RHYTHM_REDUCED, STATE_INTERP, STATE_INTERP_CLARIFY, STATE_INTERP_TASK, STATE_INTERP_PRESENT, COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE, COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE_REDUCED, DISPATCH_RULES, EMOTIONAL_CALIB, SAFETY_HITL, WEAVE_PROTOCOL, ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL, ANTI_PATTERNS_CLARIFY, ANTI_PATTERNS_HITL, ANTI_PATTERNS_PRESENT, ANTI_PATTERNS_WEAVE, ANTI_PATTERNS_CANCEL, ANTI_PATTERNS_ERROR)
- `MODE_EXAMPLES` dict covers all 10 `PromptMode` values with mode-specific multi-turn ReAct examples
- `SCENARIO_DATA_TEMPLATES` dict covers all 10 modes with appropriate data blocks (6 with content, 4 empty)
- `AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS` (5 bands: crisis, low, neutral, positive, elevated) + affect x mode interaction matrix
- `CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS` (3 depths: 0, 1, 2) with `ClarificationDepthState` tracker
- `DOMAIN_RULES` (8 domains: health, finance, elder_care, children, legal, emergency, iot, communication) + `get_domain_rules()` function
- Back prompt (~1,800 words) with 8-section structure (IDENTITY, REACT EXECUTION PROTOCOL, TOOL SELECTION RULES, SAFETY CHECK, RESULT FORMAT, AMBIGUITY HANDLING, ANTI-PATTERNS, BUDGET) and 4 in-context examples
- Multi-intent dispatch examples teach 5 patterns (single, bundled, chained, conversational+action, pure conversation)
- Cross-section coherence verified: no assembled combination produces contradictory instructions; coherence hierarchy documented (DOMAIN_RULES > SAFETY_HITL > AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS > CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS > base PROMPT_SECTIONS)
- Token counts per mode match Section 27.13 savings analysis: weighted avg ~45% reduction vs monolithic (CLARIFY_ASK: 61%, HITL_RELAY: 79%, HITL_RESOLVE: 65%, PRESENT: 47%, WEAVE: 44%, CANCEL: 65%, ERROR: 68%, STANDARD/INTERRUPT: 4%)
- All prompt texts pass lint for placeholder interpolation (`{max_iterations}`, `{open_gaps_list}`, `{field}`, `{previous_question}`, `{task_json}`, etc.)
- `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()` 12-step assembly wired and producing correct output per mode

### Epic 18.1 -- Front PROMPT_SECTIONS: Identity, ReAct & State Interpretation

**V2 Ref:** Section 6.1 (PROMPT_SECTIONS: IDENTITY, REACT_RHYTHM, STATE_INTERP variants)

Implement the first tier of the `PROMPT_SECTIONS: dict[str, str]` dictionary (Section 26.5.1). These sections define WHO the Front LLM is, HOW it operates (ReAct rhythm), and HOW to read session state. Each section is a named string constant referenced by `MODE_SECTIONS[mode]` (Section 27.8). The full version of each section is used in heavy modes (STANDARD, INTERRUPT, CLARIFY_RESOLVE); reduced variants are used in lightweight modes (CLARIFY_ASK, HITL_RESOLVE, CANCEL). All sections are concatenated by `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()` step 1.

- [ ] **18.1.1** Implement the `IDENTITY` prompt section (~150 tokens, included in ALL 10 modes). Full production text from Section 26.5.1. Content defines: (a) "You are the Concierge -- the family's trusted advisor and conversational partner"; (b) 4 "What you ARE" bullets -- sole voice, cognitive reasoner, dispatcher; (c) 4 "What you are NOT" bullets -- not executor, not relay; (d) 5 "What you can SEE" -- Session State in prompt, chat history in messages, K0 long-term memory via recall_memory tool; (e) 3 "What you CANNOT see" -- how tasks execute, other users' private data, future tool availability; (f) 5 "Your relationship" rules -- trusted advisor not servant, match emotional register, respect DND, from user's perspective YOU are doing everything, NEVER mention "the system" / "the worker" / "the back" / "the bus". Token budget: ~150 tokens. Assembly position: always first (position 1 in assembly order per Section 26.5.4).

- [ ] **18.1.2** Implement the `REACT_RHYTHM` prompt section (full version, ~200 tokens). Used in: STANDARD, CLARIFY_RESOLVE, INTERRUPT modes. Content defines the Think-Act-Observe loop: (a) each iteration: THINK (assess), ACT (call ONE tool), OBSERVE (read result); (b) iteration 1 rule: "ALWAYS call acknowledge() first. Non-negotiable"; (c) iteration 2+ rules: recall_memory if past context needed, update_beliefs if new facts, dispatch_task if user wants action; (d) final iteration rule: "Generate text response with NO tool calls. This ends your turn"; (e) typical turn: 3-5 iterations with example sequence (acknowledge -> recall_memory -> update_beliefs/update_scoreboard -> dispatch_task -> text response); (f) short turn: 2 iterations (acknowledge -> text response) for greetings, simple answers, emotional support; (g) budget: "Maximum {max_iterations} iterations per turn" -- the `{max_iterations}` placeholder is interpolated by DynamicPromptBuilder from MAX_ITERATIONS_TABLE[mode] (Section 27.6); (h) re-invocation rule: "On task_complete / weave / hitl triggers: Do NOT call acknowledge() -- there is no user input to ack. Go directly to cognitive tools or text response." Token budget: ~200 tokens. Assembly position: 2 (per Section 26.5.4).

- [ ] **18.1.3** Implement the `REACT_RHYTHM_REDUCED` prompt section (short version, ~80 tokens). Used in: CLARIFY_ASK, HITL_RESOLVE, CANCEL modes. Content: "Short turn. Follow this pattern: (1) acknowledge() if triggered by user input; (2) 0-1 cognitive tools, only if genuinely needed; (3) Text response with NO tool calls, ends your turn. Budget: Maximum {max_iterations} iterations. Keep it brief and focused. Do NOT call acknowledge() on task_complete, weave, or hitl triggers." This is the lightweight alternative to REACT_RHYTHM -- same loop but constrained to 2-3 iterations. The `{max_iterations}` placeholder is interpolated from the same MAX_ITERATIONS_TABLE. Token budget: ~80 tokens. Assembly position: 2 (same slot as REACT_RHYTHM; MODE_SECTIONS determines which variant).

- [ ] **18.1.4** Implement the `STATE_INTERP` prompt section (full version, ~200 tokens). Used in: STANDARD, CLARIFY_RESOLVE, INTERRUPT modes. Content teaches the LLM how to READ Session State data injected into the prompt: (a) `affective_now` interpretation guide -- 4 quadrants: (valence < -0.5 AND arousal > 0.7) = distress -> calm/structured/decisive, (valence < -0.3 AND arousal < 0.4) = low -> gentle/brief, (valence > 0.5 AND arousal > 0.6) = excited -> match energy, (valence near 0, arousal near 0.5) = neutral -> efficient/informative; (b) `beliefs_active` confidence thresholds -- >= 0.8 treat as fact, 0.5-0.8 likely true, < 0.5 uncertain/confirm; (c) `task_state` status interpretation -- DISPATCHED/IN_PROGRESS = running, SUSPENDED = paused for input (prioritize), COMPLETED = present results, CANCELLED = confirm, FAILED = explain gracefully; (d) `clarifications` -- blocking_gaps > 0 means MUST ask user before dispatching, helpful/minor gaps dispatch anyway. Token budget: ~200 tokens. Assembly position: 3.

- [ ] **18.1.5** Implement the 3 mode-specific `STATE_INTERP` variants (~60 tokens each). (a) `STATE_INTERP_CLARIFY`: used in CLARIFY_ASK mode. Content: "clarifications: blocking_gaps > 0 means you MUST ask the user before dispatching. Focus on the highest-severity gap first. One question at a time. Open gaps: {open_gaps_list}" -- the `{open_gaps_list}` placeholder is interpolated by DynamicPromptBuilder from `ss.clarifications.get_blocking_list()`. (b) `STATE_INTERP_TASK`: used in HITL_RESOLVE mode. Content: "task_state: SUSPENDED = a task is paused waiting for user input. This is your TOP priority. Read the pending_hil to determine what kind of input is needed. Parse the user's answer and confirm before relaying resolution." (c) `STATE_INTERP_PRESENT`: used in PRESENT mode. Content: "task_state: COMPLETED = results are available below. Present them naturally in your voice. Don't list raw data -- interpret, contextualize, highlight what matters. task_artifacts: Durable outputs (bookings, appointments, documents). Mention confirmation numbers and key details the user will need." Assembly position: 3 (same slot as STATE_INTERP; MODE_SECTIONS determines which variant). Each variant is a focused subset of STATE_INTERP, keeping only the SS sections relevant to that mode.

- [ ] **18.1.6** Implement the `COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE` prompt section (full version, ~150 tokens). Used in: STANDARD, INTERRUPT modes. Content: (a) gate question: "Before calling ANY cognitive tool, ask yourself: 'Would a competent human assistant need to WRITE THIS DOWN to remember it?' If no -- DO NOT call the tool"; (b) `update_beliefs` rules: "ONLY when user states a NEW fact not already in beliefs_active, CORRECTS an existing belief, or states a preference affecting FUTURE turns. Do NOT store greetings, obvious context, or re-state existing beliefs"; (c) `update_scoreboard` rules: "ONLY when user changes topic, uses an ambiguous pronoun that Phase 1 didn't resolve, or asks a new question"; (d) `refine_affect` rules: "ONLY when Phase 1 got it WRONG. If Phase 1 says 'neutral' and user seems neutral, leave it. Override for: sarcasm, irony, mixed emotions, masked frustration, excitement read as calm"; (e) `update_narrative` rules: "ONLY on actual thread switches or resumptions. If user continues the same topic, do NOT call this"; (f) rule of thumb: "0-2 cognitive tools per turn, not 5-6." Token budget: ~150 tokens. Assembly position: 4. Coherence note: this section constrains tool usage -- it must NOT conflict with REACT_RHYTHM which describes WHEN to call tools. Resolution: REACT_RHYTHM defines the loop structure and ordering; COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE defines the threshold for WHETHER a cognitive tool is needed. They are complementary, not contradictory.

- [ ] **18.1.7** Implement the `COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE_REDUCED` prompt section (~50 tokens). Used in: CLARIFY_RESOLVE mode. Content: "Keep it light. Call update_beliefs ONLY if the user stated a genuinely new fact or corrected something. Call update_clarifications ONLY to mark a gap as resolved. Do not over-tool a simple clarification answer." This is the lightweight version -- same principle as COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE but without the detailed per-tool rules. Coherence with REACT_RHYTHM: compatible because CLARIFY_RESOLVE uses full REACT_RHYTHM (not reduced), and this section simply relaxes the cognitive gate for the clarification-resolution flow. Assembly position: 4 (same slot as COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE).

### Epic 18.2 -- Front PROMPT_SECTIONS: Dispatch, Safety & Behavioral Rules

**V2 Ref:** Section 6.1 (PROMPT_SECTIONS: DISPATCH_RULES, EMOTIONAL_CALIB, SAFETY_HITL, COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE)

Implement the second tier of `PROMPT_SECTIONS` covering dispatch rules, emotional calibration, safety/HITL relay, and the weave protocol. These sections define WHAT the Front LLM dispatches, HOW it matches emotional register, WHEN it enforces safety bands, and HOW it weaves async results. DISPATCH_RULES and SAFETY_HITL are the two largest sections (~350 and ~300 tokens respectively) and are only included in heavy modes (STANDARD, CLARIFY_RESOLVE, INTERRUPT + HITL modes for SAFETY_HITL). EMOTIONAL_CALIB is included in ALL 10 modes to ensure consistent emotional matching regardless of prompt mode.

- [ ] **18.2.1** Implement the `DISPATCH_RULES` prompt section (~350 tokens). Used in: STANDARD, CLARIFY_RESOLVE, INTERRUPT modes. Content defines: (a) dispatch trigger verbs: "search, book, create, schedule, send, draft, buy, compare, check, look up, find, remind, order, cancel, modify, track, set up, configure, or any action verb implying work"; (b) non-dispatch cases: "greetings, emotional support, casual chat, opinions, clarification questions, 'how are you' messages"; (c) multi-intent handling rules -- independent intents ("book hotel AND search restaurants"): bundle in ONE `dispatch_task.intents[]` array; sequential intents ("book hotel THEN find restaurants near it"): two `dispatch_task` calls with `depends_on=first_task_id`; (d) reference resolution protocol (Front's responsibility, 5-step cascade): (1) check `scoreboard.referent_updates` from Phase 1, (2) check `task_artifacts` for recent completed items, (3) check `beliefs_active` for stated preferences, (4) check chat history in messages (last 2-3 turns), (5) if STILL ambiguous: pass as unresolved in `reference_context` and let the system ask for clarification; (e) domain hints requirement: "Always include domain hints (travel, health, productivity, finance, creative, shopping, family, iot, communication, elder_care)." Token budget: ~350 tokens. Assembly position: 5. Coherence note: this section tells the LLM WHEN to dispatch; COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE tells it WHEN to use cognitive tools; they are complementary (dispatch is for actions, cognitive tools are for state updates). The multi-intent rules here must be consistent with the in-context examples in MODE_EXAMPLES[STANDARD].

- [ ] **18.2.2** Implement the `EMOTIONAL_CALIB` prompt section (~100 tokens, included in ALL 10 modes). Content defines 6 emotional response strategies: (a) calm/neutral: "Efficient, informative, light personality"; (b) stressed/anxious: "Structured, decisive, calming. Reduce options. Lead with action"; (c) excited/happy: "Match energy. Celebrate. Be enthusiastic"; (d) frustrated/angry: "Acknowledge feeling first, then act. No platitudes"; (e) sad/low energy: "Gentle, shorter responses. Don't force cheerfulness"; (f) panicking: "Calm, numbered options. 'Deep breath. Here are your options.'" Token budget: ~100 tokens. Assembly position: 6. Coherence note: this section provides the BASE emotional matching strategy; AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS (Epic 18.4) provides OVERRIDE modifiers for specific affect bands. Resolution: EMOTIONAL_CALIB is always present and sets the general principle; AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS adds a more specific, actionable modifier when affect is non-neutral. The AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS text does NOT contradict EMOTIONAL_CALIB -- it SHARPENS the same intent with concrete behavioral rules (e.g., "crisis" block says "Lead with ACTION, not empathy monologue" which is the same as "Structured, decisive" from EMOTIONAL_CALIB but more specific).

Also...'") -- these are compatible with WEAVE_PROTOCOL because they refine the transition style, not the protocol itself.

### Epic 18.3 -- Front PROMPT_SECTIONS: Anti-Pattern Guards

**V2 Ref:** Section 6.1 (ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL + 5 mode-specific subsets)

Implement the 7 anti-pattern prompt sections in `PROMPT_SECTIONS`. Anti-pattern sections are mode-specific negative instruction sets that tell the LLM what NEVER to do. Each mode gets exactly ONE anti-pattern variant via `MODE_SECTIONS` (Section 27.8). The full variant (`ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL`, ~150 tokens) is used in STANDARD and INTERRUPT; lightweight variants (~50-60 tokens each) are used in other modes. Anti-pattern sections are assembled at position 9 in the 16-layer order (Section 26.5.4). Critical coherence rule: anti-pattern rules must not contradict the positive instructions in other sections of the same assembled prompt. For example, `ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL` says "Do not parrot results verbatim" which is COMPATIBLE with `STATE_INTERP` which says "Present results naturally" -- both push toward interpretation over relay.

Used in: STANDARD, INTERRUPT modes. 12 rules: (1) "Execute capabilities, spawn agents, or run workflows yourself"; (2) "Show raw JSON, error codes, HTTP status, or internal identifiers"; (3) "Say 'API error', '500', 'timeout', 'null', or 'undefined'"; (4) "Parrot structured results verbatim. Interpret and present in your voice"; (5) "Promise a specific timeline ('it'll be done in 3 seconds')"; (6) "Mention 'the worker', 'the back', 'the system', or 'the bus'"; (7) "Ignore pending HITL requests. A suspended task is your TOP priority"; (8) "Dispatch a task AND hallucinate the expected result. Wait for actual results. Do not make up outcomes"; (9) "Call dispatch_task with empty or vague intents. Be specific"; (10) "Override DND or no-interrupt rules for non-URGENT matters"; (11) "Reveal cross-member private data. (Jordan's private note about Alex's eating is used, NEVER disclosed.)"; (12) "Call acknowledge() on task_complete, weave, or hitl triggers." Coherence: rule 4 ("don't parrot") aligns with STATE_INTERP_PRESENT ("present naturally") and EMOTIONAL_CALIB ("interpret, contextualize"). Rule 8 ("don't hallucinate results") aligns with DISPATCH_RULES ("wait for actual results"). No contradictions.

### Epic 18.4 -- Front Dynamic Overlay Blocks: Affect, Depth & Domain

**V2 Ref:** Section 6.1 (AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS, CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS, DOMAIN_RULES prompt text)

Implement the three dynamic overlay block systems that are appended to the assembled prompt AFTER the base PROMPT_SECTIONS and MODE_EXAMPLES (Section 26.5.4, assembly positions 11-13). These overlays are MODIFIERS that refine the base sections without contradicting them. The coherence hierarchy is: DOMAIN_RULES (highest priority, safety constraints) > SAFETY_HITL (safety bands) > AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS (emotional modifiers) > CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS (clarification strategy) > base PROMPT_SECTIONS (default behavior). When an overlay modifies a behavior defined in a base section, the overlay takes precedence for THAT specific behavior while the rest of the base section remains active. For example: AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS "crisis" says "Shorter response. Every word must earn its place" which overrides the default response length from EMOTIONAL_CALIB, but does NOT override DISPATCH_RULES or SAFETY_HITL. DOMAIN_RULES "health" says "NEVER diagnose" which adds a constraint that no other section can override.

Fields: `field: str` (gap field name, e.g. "dates", "budget", "hotel_name"), `depth: int = 0` (0 = first ask, 1 = re-ask, 2 = final attempt), `previous_questions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)` (history of questions asked for this gap), `max_depth: int = 2` (after this, pick best option or escalate). State is tracked per gap field in `ss.clarifications`. When `update_clarifications` records a new blocking gap, depth starts at 0. When Front asks about the gap and the user's answer is incomplete (gap remains blocking), depth increments to 1. On second incomplete answer, depth increments to 2. At depth 2, Front must proceed with best guess per CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS[2]. If `depth > max_depth` is ever reached (shouldn't happen), force dispatch with whatever context is available.

### Epic 18.7 -- Section Coherence: Cross-Section Contradiction Prevention

**V2 Ref:** Section 6.1 (coherence hierarchy: DOMAIN_RULES > SAFETY_HITL > AFFECT > CLARIFY > base)

This is the critical epic that addresses the user's primary concern: when multiple prompt sections are dynamically assembled, they must NOT produce contradictory instructions. For example, if EMOTIONAL_CALIB says "be enthusiastic" for excited users, while ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL says "don't be verbose", and AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS "positive" says "can be slightly longer" -- these must all work together, not fight each other. The resolution is a strict coherence hierarchy and explicit cross-section audit. Coherence hierarchy (highest to lowest priority): (1) DOMAIN_RULES -- safety constraints that NOTHING can override (health: never diagnose, emergency: safety first); (2) SAFETY_HITL -- safety band classifications (GREEN/AMBER/RED); (3) AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS -- emotional modifiers that SHARPEN base sections; (4) CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS -- clarification strategy for the current ask; (5) base PROMPT_SECTIONS -- default behavioral instructions. When two layers address the same behavior, the higher-priority layer wins for THAT specific behavior while all other instructions from the lower layer remain active.

- [ ] **18.7.1** Document and enforce the coherence hierarchy across all assembled prompt combinations. (a) DOMAIN_RULES override all: health domain says "NEVER diagnose" -- this cannot be overridden by any affect tone, clarification depth, or base section. Emergency domain says "provide emergency numbers IMMEDIATELY" -- this overrides even CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS ("don't ask again, just proceed"). (b) SAFETY_HITL overrides affect and base: the GREEN/AMBER/RED classification persists regardless of emotional state. A crisis user who wants to delete their account still gets RED refusal -- crisis AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS changes HOW the refusal is delivered (calm, structured) but not WHETHER it happens. (c) AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS override base section tone: crisis block says "lead with ACTION, not empathy monologue" which overrides EMOTIONAL_CALIB's general guidance for stressed users. The AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS are MORE SPECIFIC so they win for tone and response length. (d) CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS override base clarification approach but are overridden by affect: depth 0 says "let user answer freely" but crisis affect says "ask YES/NO instead" -- crisis wins per hierarchy. (e) base PROMPT_SECTIONS provide default behavior: REACT_RHYTHM, COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE, DISPATCH_RULES etc. are the fallback when no higher-priority override applies. Implement a `CoherenceValidator` class that, given a `PromptMode` + `AffectBand` + `domain`, identifies any potential contradictions in the assembled text and logs warnings.

- [ ] **18.7.2** Audit all affect x base section interactions for contradictions. Enumerate and resolve: (a) ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL rule "don't parrot results verbatim" vs EMOTIONAL_CALIB "be enthusiastic" and AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS "positive": RESOLUTION -- "don't parrot" means don't copy-paste structured data; "be enthusiastic" means interpret WITH personality. These are complementary: interpret enthusiastically, don't copy-paste enthusiastically. (b) COGNITIVE_DISCIPLINE "0-2 cognitive tools per turn" vs crisis AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS "shorter response, every word must earn its place": COMPATIBLE -- crisis makes fewer tools MORE likely because the goal is fast action, not extensive state updates. crisis also reduces max_iterations (from 6 to 4 in STANDARD). (c) DISPATCH_RULES "include domain hints" vs emergency DOMAIN_RULES "provide emergency numbers IMMEDIATELY": RESOLUTION -- in emergency, skip dispatch entirely for immediate response. Emergency domain overrides dispatch flow. (d) EMOTIONAL_CALIB "match energy, be enthusiastic" vs ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL "don't promise specific timelines": COMPATIBLE -- enthusiasm is about TONE, not about making false promises. "That's awesome! I'll get started on that right away!" (enthusiastic, no timeline). (e) REACT_RHYTHM "ALWAYS call acknowledge() first" vs task_complete triggers "Do NOT call acknowledge()": NOT a contradiction -- the rule is mode-dependent. User-input modes: acknowledge. System-trigger modes (PRESENT, WEAVE, ERROR): no acknowledge. The MODE_EXAMPLES demonstrate the correct behavior.

- [ ] **18.7.3** Audit all domain x mode + section interactions for contradictions. Enumerate and resolve: (a) elder_care domain "max 3 options" vs HITL_RELAY selection with 5+ options: RESOLUTION -- elder_care domain rule takes priority. If HITL_RELAY receives 5 options but domain is elder_care, Front presents top 3 only with "there are a few more if you'd like to see them." (b) children domain "route through parent profile" vs STANDARD DISPATCH_RULES "dispatch when user wants something done": RESOLUTION -- dispatch proceeds but with `member_context.requires_parent_approval = true` flag. The orchestrator handles routing to parent. Front tells the child user: "I'll check with your parents on that!" (c) finance domain "exact amounts, never round" vs PRESENT mode "interpret and present in your voice": COMPATIBLE -- interpretation means contextualizing ("That's about a day's work budget" IS allowed as ADDITION), but the exact amount must ALSO be stated ("$87.43 on your Amex ending 4242"). (d) health domain "NEVER diagnose" vs any mode: this is an ABSOLUTE constraint. No mode, affect, or depth overrides it. Implement as a pre-dispatch check in `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()` that adds the domain rule LAST in assembly to ensure it's the final instruction the LLM reads (recency bias).

- [ ] **18.7.4** Implement runtime coherence validation in `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()`. Add a validation step between assembly and return (after step 11, before step 12): (a) scan the assembled `system_prompt` for known contradiction patterns using regex (e.g., "always" + "never" for the same action within 200 tokens); (b) check that the DOMAIN_RULES block (if present) appears AFTER all base sections in the assembled text (leveraging LLM recency bias so domain constraints are freshest in context); (c) verify that AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS appear AFTER EMOTIONAL_CALIB so the specific modifier is read after the general rule; (d) verify ANTI_PATTERNS variant matches the mode (e.g., STANDARD mode should have ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL, not ANTI_PATTERNS_CLARIFY); (e) log a structured coherence report: `{"mode": mode.value, "affect": affect_band.band, "domain": domain, "sections_assembled": section_keys, "overlays_applied": [...], "coherence_warnings": [...]}`. This validation is a development-time safety net, not a production performance gate -- it can be disabled via config flag `ENABLE_COHERENCE_VALIDATION = True/False`.

### Epic 18.8 -- Back System Prompt Sections

**V2 Ref:** Section 6.2 (Back prompt: 8 sections, ~1800 words)

Implement the `BACK_SYSTEM_PROMPT` constant string (Section 26.6). Unlike the Front prompt which is dynamically assembled per mode, the Back prompt is a MONOLITHIC string with a constant identity section (~1,500 words) plus dynamic placeholders for task-specific data (`{task_json}`, `{beliefs_summary}`, etc.). The Back LLM (Gemini) operates in JSON-only mode: all output must be tool calls, never free-form text. The prompt has 8 sections that are ALWAYS present (no mode-driven assembly needed per Section 27.14). Chat history (last 2-3 turns) is passed as real messages in the messages array.

- [ ] **18.8.1** Implement the Back IDENTITY section. Content: "You are the Worker. You receive structured task dispatches and produce structured JSON results. You are a pure executor." 4 subsections: (a) "What you ARE" -- 3 bullets: task executor with universal capability registry access, planner for multi-step execution within a single task, quality gate that validates results before submitting. (b) "What you are NOT" -- 3 bullets: not a conversationalist (NEVER produce text for human consumption; final_answer is TECHNICAL SUMMARY for presentation system), not a decision-maker on user preferences (those are in the dispatch), not aware of who the user is (serves the dispatch, not a person). (c) "What you produce" -- tool calls only, each iteration exactly ONE tool call, NOTHING else (no greetings, opinions, personality). (d) `final_answer` format guidance: "GOOD: 'Found 3 Italian restaurants in Sonoma with outdoor seating. Top match: Oenotri, 4.6 stars, $$$, available June 15.' BAD: 'Great news! I found some amazing restaurants you'll love!' The presenter decides tone. You provide data."

- [ ] **18.8.2** Implement the REACT EXECUTION PROTOCOL section (8-step mandatory sequence). Step 1 ORIENT: read task dispatch (intents, params, reference_context), read beliefs_summary and task_artifacts, verify reference_context against beliefs (if contradicts high-confidence belief >= 0.8, prefer the belief; if refers to unknown entity, call recall_memory() to verify). Step 2 CHECK EXISTING WORK: check task_artifacts for duplicate work (don't re-book if booking exists, don't re-search if results exist). Step 3 ASSESS CAPABILITY KNOWLEDGE: if capability name is known (LOW tier or obvious) -> skip to Step 5; if unknown -> Step 4. Step 4 DISCOVER: call `discover_capabilities(intent, domain)`, observe result, read each capability (name, required_params, side_effects), select best match, if none match -> `submit_result(needs_human, clarification, "No capability found for: <intent>")`. Step 5 SAFETY CHECK: check capability's side_effects flag -- GREEN (side_effects=false): execute freely; AMBER (side_effects=true): request approval FIRST via `submit_result(needs_human, approval)` with explicit consequences, WAIT for approval; RED (safety_band="RED"): refuse via `submit_result(needs_human, clarification, "This action requires elevated authorization")`, NEVER execute. Default for unknown side_effects: treat as AMBER. Step 6 INVOKE: call `invoke_capability(capability, params)`, observe result, if failed check if retry makes sense (different params, not same), max 1 retry per capability. Step 7 EVALUATE: results sufficient -> Step 8; need more data -> return to Step 3; ambiguous results -> `submit_result(needs_human, selection, options)`. Step 8 SUBMIT: call `submit_result(result_type="complete")` with final_answer (technical, 1-3 sentences), results (structured data array), artifacts_created (durable outputs).

- [ ] **18.8.3** Implement the TOOL SELECTION RULES section. 6 tools with when/when-not guidance: (a) `recall_memory(query)`: WHEN task needs historical context the dispatch doesn't provide ("What hotel did they stay at last time?"); WHEN NOT the dispatch already includes the info in params or reference_context; CALL early (Step 1). (b) `discover_capabilities(intent, domain)`: WHEN you don't know the capability name; WHEN NOT capability is obvious; CALL Step 4, once per unique intent, don't re-discover. (c) `invoke_capability(capability, params)`: WHEN you know the capability and have params; CALL Step 6, one at a time, observe before next. (d) `spawn_via_fabric(spec)`: WHEN task requires specialist agent (MEDIUM/HIGH tier only); WHEN NOT a single invoke_capability can handle it. (e) `execute_workflow(workflow_id, params)`: WHEN task has registered workflow (MEDIUM/HIGH tier only); WHEN NOT ad-hoc tasks. (f) `submit_result(result_type, ...)`: WHEN task is done OR you need human input; CALL ALWAYS at the end, this is the ONLY exit, no exceptions.

- [ ] **18.8.4** Implement the SAFETY CHECK section with detailed GREEN/AMBER/RED capability classification. GREEN (side_effects=false): "Execute freely. Examples: search, lookup, compare, recall, summarize, get status, read calendar, check weather, query inventory, list options." AMBER (side_effects=true): "Request approval FIRST. Call submit_result(result_type='needs_human', hil_type='approval') with explicit consequences in side_effects[]. WAIT for approval before executing. Examples: book accommodation, place order, send message, create event, turn on smart oven, lock door, modify calendar, transfer money." RED (safety_band="RED" in dispatch constraints): "Refuse. Call submit_result(needs_human, clarification, 'This action requires elevated authorization: <reason>.'). NEVER execute RED capabilities." Default rule: "If discover_capabilities returned a capability with side_effects=true and safety_band is not specified: treat as AMBER by default." Coherence with Front SAFETY_HITL: Front's GREEN/AMBER/RED classification MATCHES Back's classification. Front tells the user what will happen ("I'll book X -- confirm?"); Back enforces the approval gate. They must agree on which actions are GREEN vs AMBER vs RED.

Front tools: `acknowledge(message="Booking first, then I'll find restaurants nearby!")`, `dispatch_task(intents=[{action: "book hotel", params: {hotel: "Vineyard Inn"}}])`, `dispatch_task(intents=[{action: "search restaurants", params: {near: "$task-prev.result.address"}}], depends_on="task-prev")`. TWO dispatch calls because the second depends on the first's result. The `depends_on` field links them. (b) Pattern 4 -- Conversational + action: User: "Ugh I'm exhausted from the gym. Can you just book that restaurant?" Front tools: `acknowledge(message="Long day! I'll book it right now.")`, `refine_affect(emotion="tired", valence=-0.3, arousal=0.3, confidence=0.8)`, `dispatch_task(intents=[{action: "book restaurant", params: {restaurant: "Oenotri"}}], reference_context: {"that restaurant": "Oenotri"})`. Demonstrates: emotional acknowledgment + affect refinement + dispatch with reference resolution. "that restaurant" is resolved to "Oenotri" via reference_context from scoreboard/beliefs/artifacts.

- [ ] **18.9.7** Implement multi-intent dispatch example: Pattern 5 (pure conversation, no dispatch). User: "How was the weather today?" Front tools: `acknowledge(message="It was gorgeous! Sunny and 72 degrees in Napa.")`. No `dispatch_task` call. Demonstrates: the LLM must recognize when the user is NOT asking for action. Pure conversation, emotional support, opinions, and small talk do NOT trigger dispatch. This is the negative example that prevents over-dispatching. DISPATCH_RULES section explicitly lists non-dispatch cases: "greetings, emotional support, casual chat, opinions, clarification questions, 'how are you' messages." The in-context example reinforces this.

### Epic 18.10 -- DynamicPromptBuilder Integration & Front Handler Wiring

**V2 Ref:** Section 6.1 (DynamicPromptBuilder 12-step pipeline, front_handler wiring)

Wire the `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()` method (Section 27.11) into the `front_handler` (Section 27.12). The builder orchestrates all the dictionaries and overlay blocks from Epics 18.1-18.9 into a single coherent `BuiltContext` containing the assembled system prompt, chat messages, tool list, and max iterations. The front_handler calls the builder once per Front LLM invocation, passing mode, session state, envelope, affect band, clarify depth, domain, and scenario data. The builder's output feeds directly into the ReAct loop.

- [ ] **18.10.1** Implement `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()` 12-step assembly method (Section 27.11). Steps: (1) assemble prompt sections from `MODE_SECTIONS[mode]` -> list of section keys -> `PROMPT_SECTIONS[key]` for each key -> concatenate; (2) append `MODE_EXAMPLES.get(mode, "")` -- mode-specific in-context examples; (3) append `AFFECT_TONE_BLOCKS.get(affect_band.band, "")` -- affect modifier; (4) append `CLARIFY_DEPTH_BLOCKS[clarify_depth]` if mode is CLARIFY_ASK and depth is valid, interpolate `{field}` and `{previous_question}` from scenario_data; (5) append `get_domain_rules(domain)` -- domain-specific constraints; (6) append mode-specific anti-pattern subset for non-STANDARD/INTERRUPT modes (modes that use ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL already have it via step 1); (7) append `_format_scenario_data(mode, scenario_data)` -- task results, HITL data, error details; (8) append `_read_ss_sections(ss, SS_READ_CONFIGS[mode], affect_band)` -- session state context; (9) interpolate `{max_iterations}` placeholder throughout with value from `_get_max_iterations(mode, affect_band)`; (10) select tools from `TOOL_ALLOWLIST[mode]` filtered against `FRONT_TOOL_SCHEMAS`; (11) build chat history via `build_chat_history(ss, history_window, envelope)` with window from SS_READ_CONFIGS; (12) pre-call budget check -- if total tokens exceed `MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` (128K * 0.80 = 102,400), call `_compress_prompt()` (M17). Return `BuiltContext(system_prompt, messages, tools, max_iterations, mode, affect_band.band)`.

- [ ] **18.10.2** Implement `_read_ss_sections()` helper with affect-based window reduction (Section 27.11). Parameters: `ss: SessionStateManager`, `configs: list[SSReadConfig]`, `affect_band: AffectBand`. For each SSReadConfig in configs: (a) if `read_mode == "skip"`: skip entirely; (b) if section is `"history_active"`: use `config.history_window` entries, but if `affect_band.band == "crisis"`: reduce window by 5 (min 5) to save tokens in crisis; (c) if `read_mode == "slim"`: call `section.to_slim_prompt()` which returns a compressed representation (fewer fields, shorter values); (d) if `read_mode == "full"`: call `section.to_prompt()` which returns the complete representation. Format each section as `"== {section_name.upper()} ==\n{content}"`. Join all sections with `"\n\n"`. This is the largest variable-size component of the assembled prompt (~1200-5500 tokens depending on mode and SS size).

- [ ] **18.10.3** Implement `_format_scenario_data()` and `_get_max_iterations()` helpers. (a) `_format_scenario_data(mode, data)`: dispatches to mode-specific formatting using the SCENARIO_DATA_TEMPLATES patterns from Epic 18.6. For PRESENT: includes task_description, task_result_summary, artifacts. For WEAVE: includes result_count, results_summary, current_thread. For HITL_RELAY: includes hil_type, hil_question, hil_options, hil_side_effects. For HITL_RESOLVE: includes suspended_task_summary, original_question, user_answer. For ERROR: includes task_description, failure_reason, partial_results. For CANCEL: includes task_id, task_action, task_status. Returns empty string for STANDARD, CLARIFY_ASK, CLARIFY_RESOLVE, INTERRUPT. (b) `_get_max_iterations(mode, affect_band)`: looks up `MAX_ITERATIONS_TABLE[mode]` and overrides with `CRISIS_ITERATIONS_TABLE[mode]` if `affect_band.band == "crisis"`. Values: STANDARD: 6/4, CLARIFY_ASK: 3/2, CLARIFY_RESOLVE: 5/4, HITL_RELAY: 1/1, HITL_RESOLVE: 3/2, PRESENT: 3/2, WEAVE: 3/2, CANCEL: 3/2, INTERRUPT: 6/4, ERROR: 2/2.

- [ ] **18.10.4** Implement `front_handler` integration (Section 27.12). The updated `front_handler(envelope, model, ss)` flow: (1) call `determine_mode()` (from M09) passing `fsm_state`, `envelope`, `clarification_state` (open_gaps, blocking_gaps, depth), `task_state`, `affect`; (2) call `compute_affect_band(ss.affective_now.to_dict())` (from M14); (3) extract domain from `ss.control.domain_context.get("domain")` (from Phase 1 classification); (4) compute `clarify_depth` for CLARIFY_ASK mode from `ss.clarifications.get_top_blocking().get("depth", 0)`; (5) extract scenario data via `_extract_scenario_data(mode, envelope, ss)` -- this function reads envelope payload and SS to build the mode-specific data dict; (6) call `DynamicPromptBuilder().build(mode, ss, envelope, affect_band, clarify_depth, domain, scenario_data)`; (7) call `react_loop()` with `context.system_prompt`, `context.messages`, `context.tools`, `context.max_iterations`, `tool_dispatcher=front_tool_dispatcher`, `on_text_response=lambda text: emit(Envelope(...))`, `actor="front"`, `scenario=mode.value`, `trace_id=envelope.trace_id`. Return result.

- [ ] **18.10.5** Implement `_extract_scenario_data()` helper (Section 27.12). Mode-specific data extraction from envelope and SS: (a) PRESENT: `{task_description: envelope.payload.action, task_result_summary: envelope.payload.final_answer, artifacts: envelope.payload.artifacts_created}`; (b) WEAVE: `{result_count: len(ss.control.pending_results), results_summary: formatted list, current_thread: ss.narrative_active.get_active_thread_name()}`; (c) HITL_RELAY: `{hil_type, hil_question, hil_options, hil_side_effects}` from `envelope.payload`; (d) HITL_RESOLVE: `{suspended_task_summary: first SUSPENDED task's action, original_question: pending_hil.question, user_answer: envelope.payload.text}`; (e) ERROR: `{task_description, failure_reason, partial_results}` from `envelope.payload`; (f) CANCEL: `{task_id, task_action, task_status}` from envelope payload + ss.task_state lookup; (g) CLARIFY_ASK: `{gap_field, previous_question}` from `ss.clarifications.get_top_blocking()`; (h) all others: empty dict `{}`.

### Epic 18.11 -- E2E Test Suite for Prompt Assembly

**V2 Ref:** Section 14.3 (token savings validation), Appendix C.7 (prompt mode tests)

Implement comprehensive tests covering mode determination, section assembly, token budgets, overlay injection, coherence verification, and Back prompt injection (Section 27.16). Tests are integration-oriented -- they exercise the real `DynamicPromptBuilder`, real `PROMPT_SECTIONS`, real `MODE_SECTIONS`, and real overlay dictionaries. No mocking of prompt text. Test data uses realistic Session State fixtures with known affect, beliefs, and task states.

- [ ] **18.11.1** Implement `determine_mode()` unit tests covering all 10 mode paths (Section 27.16). Test cases: (a) user input + LISTENING state + no blocking gaps + no suspended tasks = STANDARD; (b) user input + CLARIFYING_WORKER state + suspended task = HITL_RESOLVE; (c) task_complete topic + DELIVERING state = PRESENT; (d) user input + CLARIFYING_USER state + blocking_gaps >= 1 = CLARIFY_ASK (when no user answer resolves the gap); (e) user input + CLARIFYING_USER state + blocking_gaps resolved by answer = CLARIFY_RESOLVE; (f) hil_request topic = HITL_RELAY; (g) async_results topic during conversation = WEAVE; (h) cancel intent detected = CANCEL; (i) user input while task IN_PROGRESS = INTERRUPT; (j) task_failed topic = ERROR. Each test constructs a minimal Envelope + FSM state + clarification state + task state and asserts the expected PromptMode.

- [ ] **18.11.2** Implement section assembly tests verifying `MODE_SECTIONS[mode]` produces the correct section set for each mode. For each of the 10 modes: (a) assert `MODE_SECTIONS[mode]` keys are a subset of `PROMPT_SECTIONS.keys()`; (b) assert the assembled prompt contains the expected section headers ("== IDENTITY ==", "== REACT RHYTHM ==", etc.); (c) assert the assembled prompt does NOT contain sections excluded by the mode (e.g., CLARIFY_ASK should NOT contain "== DISPATCH RULES ==" or "== COGNITIVE TOOL DISCIPLINE =="); (d) assert IDENTITY is always first in assembly; (e) assert EMOTIONAL_CALIB is present in all modes; (f) assert ANTI_PATTERNS variant matches the mode (STANDARD -> ANTI_PATTERNS_FULL, CLARIFY_ASK -> ANTI_PATTERNS_CLARIFY, etc.). Use `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()` with a fixture SS and assert on the output `system_prompt` string.

- [ ] **18.11.3** Implement token budget validation tests per mode against Section 27.13 savings analysis. For each mode, build the prompt with a representative SS fixture and count tokens (using tiktoken or simple word-count approximation): (a) STANDARD: ~5500 tokens (full sections + full SS); (b) CLARIFY_ASK: ~2200 tokens (61% savings from monolithic ~5700); (c) CLARIFY_RESOLVE: ~3800 tokens (33% savings); (d) HITL_RELAY: ~1200 tokens (79% savings -- lightest mode, only IDENTITY + EMOTIONAL_CALIB + SAFETY_HITL); (e) HITL_RESOLVE: ~2000 tokens (65% savings); (f) PRESENT: ~3000 tokens (47% savings); (g) WEAVE: ~3200 tokens (44% savings); (h) CANCEL: ~2000 tokens (65% savings); (i) INTERRUPT: ~5500 tokens (same as STANDARD, 4% savings); (j) ERROR: ~1800 tokens (68% savings). Assert each mode's token count is within 15% of the target. Assert weighted average savings is >= 40%.

- [ ] **18.11.4** Implement overlay injection tests for affect bands, clarify depths, and domain rules. (a) Affect: build prompt for STANDARD mode with each of the 5 affect bands (crisis, low, neutral, positive, elevated). Assert crisis prompt contains "== TONE: CRISIS MODE ==" and "max 3" and "no fluff". Assert neutral prompt does NOT contain any TONE block. Assert positive prompt contains "enthusiastic". (b) Clarify depth: build prompt for CLARIFY_ASK mode with depths 0, 1, 2. Assert depth 0 contains "FIRST ASK" and "ONE question". Assert depth 1 contains "SECOND ASK" and "{field}" placeholder is interpolated. Assert depth 2 contains "FINAL ATTEMPT" and "BEST GUESS". (c) Domain: build prompt for STANDARD mode with domain="health". Assert prompt contains "== DOMAIN: HEALTH ==" and "NEVER diagnose". Build with domain="emergency". Assert prompt contains "PRIORITY: USER SAFETY FIRST". Build with domain=None. Assert no DOMAIN block present. (d) Combined: build prompt for STANDARD + crisis + health domain. Assert ALL three overlays are present and in correct order (affect after base sections, domain after affect).

- [ ] **18.11.5** Implement coherence smoke tests verifying no contradictions in any mode + affect + domain combination. Test matrix: 10 modes x 5 affect bands x 3 representative domains (None, "health", "emergency") = 150 combinations. For each combination: (a) build the prompt via `DynamicPromptBuilder.build()`; (b) assert no "ALWAYS" followed by contradictory "NEVER" for the same action within 500 characters; (c) assert domain rules (if present) appear AFTER base EMOTIONAL_CALIB in the assembled text; (d) assert affect tone block (if present) appears AFTER EMOTIONAL_CALIB; (e) assert anti-pattern variant matches the mode; (f) assert `{max_iterations}` placeholder is fully interpolated (no raw `{max_iterations}` in output); (g) assert `{open_gaps_list}` is interpolated if mode is CLARIFY_ASK; (h) if `CoherenceValidator` (18.7.4) is enabled, assert zero coherence warnings. This is a combinatorial regression test that catches contradictions introduced by future prompt text changes.

Assert: `{task_json}` placeholder is replaced with valid JSON; `{beliefs_summary}` contains formatted beliefs; `{task_state_summary}` contains task status; `{artifacts_summary}` contains completed artifacts; `{safety_band}` is "GREEN" or "AMBER" or "RED"; `{persona_prefs}` contains user preferences; `{max_tool_calls}` is a positive integer matching tier (LOW=2, MEDIUM=5, HIGH=10 per M10 TIER_BUDGET). (b) Assert the Back prompt contains all 11 sections (8 structural + 3 injection blocks): "== IDENTITY ==", "== REACT EXECUTION PROTOCOL ==", "== TOOL SELECTION RULES ==", "== SAFETY CHECK ==", "== RESULT FORMAT ==", "== AMBIGUITY HANDLING ==", "== ANTI-PATTERNS ==", "== BUDGET ==", "== IN-CONTEXT EXAMPLES ==", "== TASK DISPATCH ==", "== SESSION CONTEXT ==". (c) Assert the Back prompt does NOT contain user-facing language ("I'll help", "Great news", "Don't worry"). (d) Assert total Back prompt size is ~1,800 words + task_json overhead.

## M19 -- End-to-End Integration & "One Ordinary Day" Demo

**Goal:** Execute the complete "One Ordinary Day" 30-turn demo storyline end-to-end with real LLM calls, validating all architecture features across 7 acts with the Smith family.
**Design Sections (V2):** 13 (Scenarios: 7 end-to-end walkthroughs A-G, architecture feature coverage map), 14.2 (validation goals)
**Depends On:** M01-M18 (ALL prior milestones)
**Exit Criteria:**

- All 30 turns of the demo storyline execute end-to-end with real LLM calls.
- All 7 acts complete: Before Dawn, Morning Machine, Midday Pivot, Crisis Hour, Afternoon Weave, Evening, Night Mode.
- All architecture features demonstrated: Front/Back split, acknowledge-first, multi-intent dispatch, recall_memory (episodic/semantic/procedural), HITL (approval/selection/clarification), WEAVE (single/dual/triple), IoT monitors (LAUNDRY/DOORBELL/THERMOSTAT/OVEN), device-based identity, affect tracking, crisis management, NO INTERRUPT rule, DND enforcement, cross-member privacy, elder care, parent-relayed child requests.
- All 12 validation goals from Section 12 are met.
- Demo runs as an interactive session with real Gemini LLM calls.

- [ ] **19.1.2** Create family member profiles and device registry

  **File:** `poc/k1_poc/demo/family.py`

  ```python
  """
  Smith family profiles for the demo.

  Device-based identity: each device maps to a family member.
  FamilyOS knows who is typing based on which device the message
  originates from -- NOT voice recognition.

  Members:
      Alex (38)    -- iPhone (primary), MacBook (work). Full adult access.
      Jordan (36)  -- Android phone (primary). Full adult access.
      Riley (8)    -- NO device. No direct access. Parents relay.
      Nana Liz (67) -- iPad (simplified). Limited access, wellness.
  """
  from dataclasses import dataclass, field

  @dataclass
  class FamilyMember:
      name: str
      age: int
      role: str
      devices: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
      access_level: str = "full"  # full, limited, none
      persona_key: str = ""
      dnd_active: bool = False

  SMITH_FAMILY: dict[str, FamilyMember] = {
      "alex": FamilyMember(
          name="Alex", age=38, role="Software engineer, WFH",
          devices=["iphone-alex", "macbook-alex"],
          access_level="full", persona_key="alex_persona",
      ),
      "jordan": FamilyMember(
          name="Jordan", age=36, role="Pediatric nurse",
          devices=["android-jordan"],
          access_level="full", persona_key="jordan_persona",
      ),
      "riley": FamilyMember(
          name="Riley", age=8, role="3rd grader",
          devices=[],  # NO device -- parents relay
          access_level="none", persona_key="riley_profile",
      ),
      "nana_liz": FamilyMember(
          name="Nana Liz", age=67, role="Jordan's mother",
          devices=["ipad-nana"],
          access_level="limited", persona_key="nana_liz_persona",
      ),
  }

  DEVICE_TO_MEMBER: dict[str, str] = {
      "iphone-alex": "alex",
      "macbook-alex": "alex",
      "android-jordan": "jordan",
      "ipad-nana": "nana_liz",
  }

  def identify_member(device_id: str) -> str | None:
      """Device-based identity resolution."""
      return DEVICE_TO_MEMBER.get(device_id)
  ```

### Epic 19.9 -- Validation Goals (Section 12)

**V2 Ref:** Section 14.2 (what this POC validates)

- [ ] **19.9.1** Validate: Bus-driven actor coordination works (two LLMs, no shared loop)

  Verified across all 30 turns: Front handles conversation flow, Back handles capability execution. No shared event loop. All coordination through K1 bus envelopes.

- [ ] **19.9.2** Validate: Causal ordering replaces anti-spin (TimingChain parent_id chains)

  Verified: every dispatch -> task.complete -> present chain has parent_id linking. No polling, no spin-wait. Demonstrated clearly in Turns 1, 4, 9, 21, 24.

- [ ] **19.9.3** Validate: Session State as shared memory eliminates amnesia

  Verified across acts: beliefs about diorama (T3) persist through T27-28. Jordan's wake preferences (T2) persist through T30. Alex's demo stress (T21) contexts T23-24. Laundry thread (T11) persists through T14.

- [ ] **19.9.4** Validate: Tool distribution follows real K1 taxonomy (Front: Signal+Cognitive+Read+Control, Back: Action+Read+Control)

  Verified: Demo exercises Front tools: acknowledge, dispatch_task, refine_affect, update_beliefs, update_scoreboard, update_clarifications, update_narrative, recall_memory (1 signal + 5 cognitive + 1 shared read + 1 control). Demo exercises Back tools: invoke_capability, submit_result, recall_memory (1 action + 1 control + 1 shared read). Full catalog: 10 Front + 6 Back (14 total, recall_memory shared actor='both'). No crossover between Front-only and Back-only tools.

- [ ] **19.9.5** Validate: Both actors use shared react_loop()

  Verified: Front and Back both run through the same ReAct loop with different tool sets and termination conditions.

- [ ] **19.9.6** Validate: Concurrent conversation is possible (Front handles input while Back works)

  Verified at Turn 14 (Alex talks while Back processes) and Turn 24 (Alex converses while 3 async results queue). Front is never blocked by Back execution.

- [ ] **19.9.7** Validate: Weave Protocol works (async results merged naturally)

  Verified: T15 (dual weave: Marcus reply + Nana Liz), T24 (triple weave: shift swap + grocery ETA + school alert). WeaveBatcher collects in 500ms windows, Front invoked once per batch.

- [ ] **19.9.8** Validate: Task lifecycle management works (cancel, suspend, resume, chain, bundle)

  Verified: HITL suspension in T5-6 (grocery approval), T9-10 (message approval), T20 (shift swap edit). Multi-intent bundles in T2, T4, T14, T16, T19, T25. Task rescheduling in T14.

- [ ] **19.9.9** Validate: FrontLock prevents race conditions

  Verified: when WEAVE results arrive during Front LLM generation, they queue and drain after current response completes. Demonstrated in T15, T24.

- [ ] **19.9.10** Validate: invoke_capability() is the universal executor (domain-agnostic)

  Verified across 7 domains: productivity (T7-8), family (T2), health (T16), shopping (T4-6), IoT (T3,T17), communication (T9-10,T19), elder care (T15-16). Same invoke_capability for all.

- [ ] **19.9.11** Validate: Session coherence under concurrency (Single Writer + DeltaAggregator)

  Verified: when Jordan logs in (T18), her session reads are consistent with writes from Alex's session (T1-16). DeltaAggregator batched all Back writes. No corruption from concurrent sessions.

- [ ] **19.9.12** Validate: K1 bus infrastructure is production-ready for this pattern

  Verified: 30 turns, 7 acts, 3 active users, 50+ bus events, IoT monitors firing asynchronously, WEAVE batching, multi-intent dispatch -- all flowing through K1 bus without deadlock, message loss, or ordering violations.
